problems.text: No skill walks a release: the flow lives as prose in `.claude/rules/releases.md`, assumes one package, and never says why `release.yml` and `release-tag.yml` are separate or why `apm/apm.yml` is kmctl's version source
`.claude/rules/releases.md` will describe a stale one-package flow once releases take a package and the notes are committed in the version pull request, and it would repeat the skill's steps
No test reads `.claude/skills/`, so a repo-local skill that names a renamed workflow input or a moved file goes stale silently

goals.text: An operator or agent releases kmctl or kmaudit by naming the package, and every release goes out with notes that were reviewed before merge and checked after publish
The always-loaded release rule and the skill do not repeat each other, and the skill stays true to the workflows it drives

outcomes.change: `/release <kmctl|kmaudit>` walks the dry run, the real run, the notes review in the version pull request and the published-notes check
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_release_skill.py` (front matter names `release`, every `-f KEY=` is a `release.yml` input, package values match the input's options, cited paths exist), and a manual `/release kmaudit` dry run

outcomes.change: `releases.md` keeps only the no-`--admin` rule and `every-release-has-notes`, reworded for notes reviewed in the pull request, and points at the skill
outcomes.checked_by: `tests/test_rules.py` (cited paths exist, cited ADRs exist) and `new:tests/test_release_skill.py` (the rule names the skill's folder `.claude/skills/release/`)

outcomes.change: A test pins the repo-local release skill to `release.yml`'s inputs and the files it cites
outcomes.checked_by: the test fails on a copy of the skill with a made-up `-f` input or a missing path, and passes on the real one
